title: FedDriftGuard adaptive federated learning with differential privacy for concept drift in edge environments
task: Federated learning with drift adaptation and differential privacy for edge environments
key_results: 9-14% accuracy, 11-17% F1 improvement over baselines; 28% shorter adaptation latency; 20-35% communication cost reduction; formal DP guarantees maintained
comments: FedDriftGuard unifies drift detection, adaptive aggregation, and DP well; drift-optimal privacy scheduler is elegant trade-off mechanism.

model_io.model: DP-DriftNet (attention-based time encoding + drift-directed weighting)
inputs: local client data under concept drift
outputs: federated model updates with DP guarantees

hypotheses.hypothesis: Attention-based encoding captures changing data patterns
Drift-optimal scheduler balances privacy-utility

task: AI-generated vs human-written text classification with adversarial robustness

comments: Identifies critical vulnerability gap between accuracy and robustness; CA emerges as best accuracy-robustness trade-off.

title: Transversely pumped laser driven particle accelerator
task: Laser-driven plasma acceleration of electrons and ions
key_results: 1.12 GeV proton beams in 3.6 mm plasma; electron acceleration gradients of ~1 TeV/m
comments: Novel transverse pumping geometry avoids dephasing limitations of conventional LWFA, though experimental validation beyond simulation is not yet demonstrated.

model_io.model: Transversely Pumped Acceleration (TPA) scheme

hypotheses.hypothesis: Tuning injection timing and beamlet spacing enables control of acceleration structure propagation orthogonal to laser direction
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via simulation; precise control achieved with tunable phase velocity

title: Experimental investigation of novel 18 multiturn multiplane pulsating heat pipe for methanol
task: Thermal performance optimization of multiturn multiplane pulsating heat pipes with methanol
key_results: 18-turn multiplane: average thermal resistance 0.3408 °C/W (vs. dry fin 0.45 °C/W); optimum orientation 60–70°; bottom heating (90°) best for heat transfer
comments: Multiplane configuration shows orientation independence, which simplifies deployment; temperature overshoot behavior at startup is well-characterized.

model_io.model: 18-turn multiplane PHP with methanol working fluid

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multiplane geometry and optimized fill ratio/orientation minimize thermal resistance; tail-slap and startup transients vary with heat load regime
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; multiplane shows orientation independence; 0.3408 °C/W achieves ~24% improvement over dry fin; startup behavior transitions from overshoot to smooth with heat load

title: Multiscale quantum-to-device simulation framework for Ca3AsBr3 perovskite solar cells: engineering efficient electron transport layers
task: Optimization of Ca₃AsBr₃ perovskite solar cells via ETL engineering
key_results: WS₂-based device: PCE 20.50%, Voc 1.165 V, Jsc 20.55 mA/cm², FF 85.64%; optimal absorber thickness 1200 nm
comments: DFT-validated bandgap (1.66 eV) and mechanical stability support the material; though PCE is competitive, stability under operation remains unreported.

model_io.model: Multiscale DFT + SCAPS-1D device simulator

hypotheses.hypothesis: WS₂ ETL with optimized thickness and low defect density yields highest efficiency due to superior band alignment and defect tolerance
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; WS₂ achieves 20.50% PCE; reduced bulk/interface defects minimize recombination

title: Design and analysis of tetra-port MIMO antenna for next generation vehicular communication
task: Tetra-port MIMO antenna design for 5G/6G vehicle-to-vehicle communication
key_results: >20 dB isolation without isolation structures; gain 3.8 dBi; efficiency 87%; envelope correlation coefficient <0.1; diversity gain >9.9 dB
comments: Compact footprint (42.44×43.56 mm) and high isolation without decoupling networks is impressive; in-vehicle EMI immunity is a practical advantage.

model_io.model: Tetra-port MIMO antenna at 5.9 GHz

hypotheses.hypothesis: Perpendicular element configuration and defected ground yield high inter-port isolation and low envelope correlation without explicit decoupling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; >20 dB isolation and ECC <0.1 achieved; diversity metrics support MIMO performance

title: Meta-lens-based circularly polarized fixed-beam antenna for high-gain wideband millimeter-wave applications
task: High-gain wideband circularly polarized mm-wave antenna design
key_results: 4 dB gain improvement with meta-lens; impedance bandwidth 24–31 GHz; axial ratio <3 dB across band
comments: Meta-lens approach is elegant for gain enhancement in compact form, though the 4 dB improvement is modest relative to the added complexity.

model_io.model: Meta-lens-based CP antenna
inputs: two meta-lens layers with subwavelength cross-shape atoms

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dual-layer meta-lens with optimized focal distance enhances gain of single-point-fed CP radiator

title: Study on the influence of inducer and its guide vanes on cryogenic cavitation and pressure fluctuation characteristics of an LNG pump
task: Inducer and guide vane optimization for cryogenic LNG pump cavitation control
key_results: Inducer raises impeller inlet pressure; head coefficient increases from 1.74 to 1.88; critical cavitation number reduced from 0.0628 to 0.041
comments: Thermodynamically modified cavitation model is appropriate for cryogenic conditions, and results show inducer is effective at delaying inception.

model_io.model: Two-stage LNG pump CFD with Zwart-Gerber-Belamri cavitation model

hypotheses.hypothesis: Inducer elevates inlet pressure and delays cavitation inception; guide vanes organize inflow and modulate pressure fluctuation periodicity
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; inducer critical for cavitation resistance; guide vanes influence local fluctuations but not outlet/diffuser

title: Dynamic characteristics and structural response of a supercavitating underwater vehicle: an experimental and numerical study
task: Structural dynamics and failure analysis of supercavitating underwater vehicles
key_results: Drag reduction with speed; cylindrical shell experiences peak stress during tail-slapping; critical frequencies to avoid: ~18 Hz (all parts), 15–16 Hz (conical–cylindrical junction)
comments: Tail-slap vibration is the dominant failure driver; reinforcement strategy is practical but experimental validation under full-scale conditions is needed.

model_io.model: Supercavitating vehicle FEM and flow towing experiment

hypotheses.hypothesis: Tail-slapping vibration induces extreme accelerations and stress concentration in cylindrical shell
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; cylindrical section identified as critical failure zone
